- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce volatility amplification.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast with sentiment’s most recent 3-period trend.
